messages.author: 009e9ca25977e9bc
messages.subject: SEM categorical item issue
parts:
Hello, I'm a bit of a novice at lavaan and SEM and was hoping for some assistance with this problem. Basically I have a SEM that was working fine, now I’ve added 4 binary items to the model (each one coded as 1 or 0) and the model dies with the following error:

Error in lavsamplestats@cov[[g]][cbind(row.idx, col.idx)] :
  subscript out of bounds
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, group.label = group.label,  :
  lavaan WARNING: exogenous variable(s) declared as ordered in data: locSZ locGD locMA locOT
2: In lav_partable_check(lavpartable, categorical = categorical, warn = TRUE) :
  lavaan WARNING: parameter table does not contain thresholds

The actual SEM model is:

modelDef <- '
Control =~ contr4 + contr6 + contr3 + contr9      # latent variable definitions
TranSuc =~ prac10 + prac7 + prac11
HCAvail =~ resoua12 + resoua11
HCDevl =~ perfor8 + perfor9
HCStr =~ confid4 + confid1 + confid3
Perform =~ perfor20 + perfor18 + perfor19


TranSuc ~ Control                                 # Model
HCStr ~ HCAvail + HCDevl
Perform ~ TranSuc + HCStr + Age + Sector + staffchil + staffhkl + locSZ + locGD + locMA + locOT
‘

With the locSZ,  locGD,  locMA, locOT fields being the categorical items. I’ve identified these in the SEM as follows as I think I need to do, but not having any joy.

modelFit <- sem(modelDef, data = dataset, ordered=c("locSZ","locGD", "locMA","locOT")
                , sample.cov = true, estimator = "WLS")


Prior to adding these 4 items it was all working fine!

Any tips would be greatly appreciated.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: SEM categorical item issue
parts:
On 12/01/2015 10:59 PM, Taman Powell wrote:

> Perform ~ TranSuc + HCStr + Age + Sector + staffchil + staffhkl + locSZ
> + locGD + locMA + locOT
>
> With the locSZ, locGD, locMA, locOT fields being the categorical
> items. I’ve identified these in the SEM as follows as I think I need to
> do, but not having any joy.
>
> |
> modelFit <-sem(modelDef,data
> =dataset,ordered=c("locSZ","locGD","locMA","locOT")
> ,sample.cov =true,estimator ="WLS")

Only endogenous (dependent) variables need to be declared as 'ordered'.
Not exogenous predictors. If they are binary (coded 0/1), you can just
leave them as they are.

See: http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/cat.html

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: SEM categorical item issue
parts:
On 12/02/2015 07:56 PM, Taman Powell wrote:
> Hi Yves,
>
> I don’t think there is any overlap with other parts of the model.
> Basically model was looking at completely different things and then had
> a query regarding whether geographic area had an impact, so setup the 4
> items to look at this. Anyway, I’m attaching the complete dataset and
> code. I really appreciate your help with this.

Ok. The estimator is the problem: "WLS". Your sample is not large enough
for this estimator. You really should use ML, or even better MLR (robust
ML). It works, I tried.

WLS (in the continuous case!) will treat all variables (including the
exogenous 0/1 variables) as stochastic and Gaussian. That will almost
certainly give problems if you include 0/1 variables...

Yves.
